body: Maintainer decision, 2026-11-22, given in the question dialog: **not now. After #2556.** Finish the cheaper speedups of #2556 first, then measure the release gate again. This issue stays open at P8.

Research result: keep the current cut gate. Compare execution methods before a change to the release workflow.

The maintainer deferred implementation until after #2556. Its approved work is #3513, #3514, and #3515. #3513 remains open. #3514 and #3515 are closed. A fresh release measurement still comes first. This research does not approve implementation or cloud spending.

## Answers to the five questions

1. **Build once and partition: yes, with limits.** Build each required profile once. Use a debug archive and a separate release archive. Use identical build features, target, filters, and nextest versions on all workers. Run ordinary tests with the default ignore selection. Run heavy tests with `--run-ignored only`. Partition each selected set with `--partition hash:k/n`.

   `xtask/src/plan.rs` defines different debug and heavy crate sets. It also defines doctests, clippy, and optional snapshot steps. One nextest archive does not replace this plan. Keep doctests under `cargo test --doc` on the cut runner. Keep clippy there too. Keep the current `--no-snapshots` rule and the local snapshot checks.

   Preserve `lanes::ISOLATED` and `lanes::alone` from `xtask/src/lanes.rs`. For the first trial, keep those complete binaries on the cut runner. Run them after its shared queue stops. A group with `max-threads = 1` only serializes that group. It does not stop unrelated tests. Nextest can reserve the full local test budget with `threads-required = "num-test-threads"`. This controls one nextest process, not other processes on the host. Keep one executor per worker. Keep the heavy-before-debug phase order from `xtask/src/queue.rs`. Wait for all heavy work before any worker starts debug work.

   Keep known-fail tests out of ordinary heavy partitions. Run their current checks once on the cut runner. `xtask/src/known_fail.rs` checks the named test, assertion location, panic prefix, and issue state. A generic expected-failure result is insufficient.

   Put UI execution under `xvfb-run -a` with the current Mesa drivers. The first slice keeps UI on the cut runner. Evidence: `.github/workflows/cut.yml` and `.claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md`.

   Public references: [Nextest archiving](https://nexte.st/docs/ci-features/archiving/), [partitioning](https://nexte.st/docs/ci-features/partitioning/), [running tests and doctests](https://nexte.st/docs/running/), [heavy test weights](https://nexte.st/docs/configuration/threads-required/), and [test groups](https://nexte.st/docs/configuration/test-groups/).

2. **One verdict requires a complete execution manifest.** Reuse the structure of `xtask/src/verdict.rs` and `xtask/src/lane_split.rs`. Do not use the current batch record unchanged. It has no archive digest, tree identity, profile identity, or list of expected test identities.

   The trusted cut runner creates the manifest. Record the run ID, commit, tree, archive SHA-256, nextest version, target, profile, selection, and expected partitions. Identify each test by profile, package, binary, and full test name. Assign each expected test exactly once. Compare the completed identities with the expected identities. Reject missing, duplicate, foreign, incomplete, canceled, timed-out, and failed results. Include the local steps in the same verdict. Do not infer completeness from counts alone.

   Retain each worker's exit status, complete output, JUnit report, and timings under `gate-logs/<run>/<profile>/<partition>/`. The collector writes one index and verdict. Keep per-test duration separate from phase wall time. Keep the existing `seconds<TAB>step name` format for `timings.tsv`. Give partition steps unique names. Do not call summed overlapping durations the gate wall time.

   [Nextest JUnit support](https://nexte.st/docs/machine-readable/junit/) documents one test case per test. Keep skipped entries out of naive report concatenation. Partition reports can otherwise repeat skipped tests. JUnit helps inspection; the manifest and executor status determine completeness.

   Related work: #2908 concerns batch lanes. `RECOMMENDED.md`, section `#2908`, rejects a full `target/` transfer because of its size. Measure compressed nextest archives and transfer time before a different choice. `docs/decisions/README.md` defines the decision record format. This checkout has no other files in that directory.

3. **Servers and payment: use existing hosts for the first comparison.** Start with the cut runner and one available Linux x86-64 host. Do not add cloud capacity before the comparison supports it. For a later cloud slice, use two workers first. Increase to four only if the total time and cost improve.

   Use a pinned Linux image with the compatible runtime libraries, nextest, Mesa, and xvfb. Keep Rust and Cargo on the build runner. Test-only workers need them only if a selected test starts Cargo. Transfer the exact source revision and fixtures with the archives. Use `--workspace-remap` when paths differ. Check CPU instruction support and system library compatibility before execution. Check required build outputs and fixtures; the archive is not a full machine image. Audit paths embedded at compile time before moving the workspace.

   Charge cloud use to the maintainer's approved project and budget. This session creates no server. The issue's approximately EUR 0.44/hour is historical evidence, not a current quote. At that historical rate, two extra workers for one billed hour cost about EUR 0.88. Include the build host, transfer, image storage, and hourly rounding in a current estimate. [Hetzner billing](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/billing/faq/) confirms hourly billing and charges for powered-off servers. Deletion must end the allocation.

4. **Safety and tree identity: keep control on the cut runner.** Workers receive public source, fixtures, and compiled tests. They receive no GitHub token, cloud token, signing key, or sccache credentials. Use a clean account and an allow-list of environment variables. The cut runner transfers inputs and collects outputs. It alone holds provisioning credentials and tag permissions.

   Pin inputs by digest. Check each worker's clean source tree before and after execution. Reject a moved checkout. `xtask/src/checkout.rs` already treats a moved checkout as void. Retain its intent across all workers. Delete workers on success, failure, cancellation, and timeout. Add independent expiry cleanup for controller failure. Confirm deletion and remove temporary volumes and addresses.

   Preserve both checks in `.github/workflows/cut.yml`: the merge has the gated tip as its second parent, and its tree equals the gated tree. Only the complete distributed verdict can publish `cut-tip.txt`. Never tag from a worker's individual success.

5. **No technical dependency on a binary split.** Nextest hashes individual tests inside existing binaries. Hash partitions balance test identities, not measured duration. One slow test remains a lower bound.

   There is a scheduling dependency on the maintainer's decision. Finish #3513 and measure again before implementation. #2556 approved cheaper changes, not a binary split.

   There is also a specific performance risk. `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings_tests.rs:57` shares a plan through `LazyLock` after #3515. [Nextest runs each test in a separate process](https://nexte.st/docs/design/why-process-per-test/). Therefore, nextest can compute that plan again for each test. Compare whole-binary libtest execution with nextest before adoption.

## Proposal and concrete follow-ups

Choose measurement first. Keep the current cut path until a complete comparison passes. Include build, packing, boot, transfer, execution, and collection in total wall time. Drop immediate four-server deployment. Drop a promised 20–25 minute gate time: the available evidence does not establish it. Reconsider nextest adoption if lost cache sharing or transfer time removes the benefit.

The follow-ups below remain blocked for maintainer review. No follow-up authorizes a release workflow change by itself.

1. **Measure archived tests on two release-gate workers**
   - Compare nextest partitions with current libtest binaries after the approved #2556 work.
   - Done means: one archived build runs on two hosts; test identities match; build, transfer, execution, total time, and cost are reported.
   - Proposed labels: P8, effort:max, area:build.
2. **Preserve release-gate coverage when workers reuse compiled tests**
   - Map debug, heavy, isolated, UI, doctest, clippy, snapshot, and known-fail work without a coverage change.
   - Done means: the selected method runs every required test once; local checks and phase order remain; isolation checks pass.
   - Proposed labels: P8, effort:high, area:build.
3. **Collect release-gate partitions with one complete verdict**
   - Bind results to the trusted manifest and retain each worker's logs and timing records.
   - Done means: the collector rejects missing, duplicate, stale, foreign, failed, and incomplete records; valid records produce one verdict.
   - Proposed labels: P8, effort:high, area:build.
4. **Run temporary release-gate workers with a bounded lifecycle**
   - Define the image, credential separation, spending limit, cleanup, and cut integration after a successful trial.
   - Done means: success, failure, cancellation, and controller failure leave no worker; only a complete verdict permits the existing tag checks.
   - Proposed labels: P8, effort:high, area:build.

## Measured local archive trial

Revision: `d486f3a3b823d48ce81a7f5e57700e158a2513df`. Nextest: `0.9.152`.
The trial used existing repository tests. It changed no source or configuration.

The first selection, `camcraft-gcode --lib`, contained no tests.
Its cold archive preparation took 312.44 s.
Nextest rejected the empty first partition with exit code 4.
That attempt is setup evidence, not a passing trial.

The corrected selection was `camcraft-gcode --test parse`.
Archive preparation took 1.94 s with the dependencies already built.
The archive contained one test binary and occupied 6,695,374 bytes.
Its SHA-256 was `fae22b3040ccab0d71371760eef934dc62871969887c1762f0f310a10375f7a6`.
Both partitions reused this same archive.

| Partition | Passed | Test execution | Command wall time | Exit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `hash:1/2` | 23 | 0.065 s | 0.14 s | 0 |
| `hash:2/2` | 14 | 0.038 s | 0.11 s | 0 |

The JSON inventory contained 37 tests.
The completed names had a union of 37, zero overlap, zero missing names, and zero unexpected names.
Both partitions ran sequentially on one host.
This proves small-scale archive reuse and partition coverage.
It does not measure two-server performance, heavy tests, UI compatibility, transfer time, or release-gate wall time.
The two-host comparison remains necessary before the original measurement condition is complete.

The trial used the official Linux nextest binary from `https://get.nexte.st/latest/linux`.
The reported version identifies this trial. A production image must pin the version and checksum.
These commands reproduce the successful selection with the same tool and source revision:

```bash
/usr/bin/time -f 'archive_wall_seconds=%e' \
  /tmp/camcraft-2557-nextest/cargo-nextest nextest archive \
  -p camcraft-gcode --test parse --locked --offline \
  --build-jobs 2 --target-dir /tmp/camcraft-2557-target \
  --archive-file /tmp/camcraft-2557-parse.tar.zst

/usr/bin/time -f 'partition_1_wall_seconds=%e' \
  /tmp/camcraft-2557-nextest/cargo-nextest nextest run \
  --archive-file /tmp/camcraft-2557-parse.tar.zst \
  --workspace-remap /home/mikekinney/CamcraftCodex \
  --partition hash:1/2 --test-threads 2 --no-fail-fast --retries 0

/usr/bin/time -f 'partition_2_wall_seconds=%e' \
  /tmp/camcraft-2557-nextest/cargo-nextest nextest run \
  --archive-file /tmp/camcraft-2557-parse.tar.zst \
  --workspace-remap /home/mikekinney/CamcraftCodex \
  --partition hash:2/2 --test-threads 2 --no-fail-fast --retries 0

/tmp/camcraft-2557-nextest/cargo-nextest nextest list \
  --archive-file /tmp/camcraft-2557-parse.tar.zst \
  --workspace-remap /home/mikekinney/CamcraftCodex \
  --message-format json
```

Local evidence remains in `/tmp/camcraft-2557-partition-1.log`, `/tmp/camcraft-2557-partition-2.log`, and `/tmp/camcraft-2557-list.json`.
These temporary files are not durable release artifacts.

The local trial reused one valid archive across two partitions.
It ran all 37 selected tests with no overlap or missing test.
